summary: Server singleton: Osiris requests to reset tutorial messages (ls::Variant alternative 7 of esv::script::RequestSystem's requests). Pushed by the Osiris call at EoCServer.dll+0x12A86B0 (two integer arguments); filled by esv::script::RequestSystem::ProcessEmitRequests. Seen.py context: singleton present in the idle level, all zero.

fields.name: RequestEntity
fields.evidence: Windows esv::script::RequestSystem variant visitor bg3.exe+0x2EA3260, case 7 (ResetTutorialsMessageRequest): appends to the singleton's array (third storage of bg3.exe+0x2EA0D50 = adder bg3.exe+0x2EA2E10) a 16-byte element whose +0 is the requester entity *param_2[1].

fields.name: UserId
fields.evidence: Same Windows case 7 copies the 8-byte esv::script::ResetTutorialsMessageRequest as one qword to +8. Its split comes from the Toolkit Osiris call EoCServer.dll+0x12A86B0: first integer argument -> request +0 (4 bytes). The notification made from it, eoc::notification::ResetTutorialsMessageRequestNotificationComponent, carries a UserId at +0 (SE Coverage.h; Windows notification builder bg3.exe+0x2DF53B0 case 0x22 copies int +0 and byte +4 of its payload) - hence the name.

fields.name: field_C
fields.evidence: Toolkit EoCServer.dll+0x12A86B0: second integer argument != 0 -> request +4 (1 byte); the notification copies one byte at +4.

fields.name: _PadD
fields.evidence: rest of the 8-byte request (copied as one qword on Windows).

fields.name: Requests
fields.evidence: Windows adder bg3.exe+0x2EA2E10 allocates 0x10 bytes, zeroes ptr and size, destructor thunk_FUN_1405946c0 (plain array free: trivial elements); RequestSystem visitor bg3.exe+0x2EA3260 case 7 appends elements of stride 0x10. Read by esv::notification::System (registration bg3.exe+0x236B740 lists it).

open_questions: The 8-byte request at element +8 is copied as one qword on Windows; its split (int32 at +8, byte at +0xC) rests on the Toolkit Osiris call and on the notification component's shape - the Windows Osiris call was not found by name (no match for EoCServer.dll+0x12A86B0).
Meaning of the flag at +0xC; Osiris function name.
status_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
second_pass: Windows code now confirms the singleton is a plain Array with 16-byte trivial elements, the requester entity at +0 and the 8-byte request at +8 (RequestSystem visitor bg3.exe+0x2EA3260 case 7, adder bg3.exe+0x2EA2E10); the int was renamed UserId after the notification it becomes. The split inside the 8-byte request is still Toolkit-only.
